title: 第070章 张念华的第一次胎动第069章 张山风的合体展示
slug: 全民修仙之系统上交囯家
content_zh:
他伸手拿起那盏灵能灯，灯的热度透过底座传到他的掌心里，像一枚正在被缓慢焐热的硬币。他把它端起来，朝台阶方向走了两步，然后停下来等她。她跟上了他的脚步，落后大约半步。张山风从门框边直起身来，端着那杯还没喝完的茶跟在她身后。四神兽依次从各自的位置站起来，白虎最后起身，它站起来的时候抖了一下尾巴，然后跟上了队列。
观星台上的灵草被风吹动了一下。风从星尘带的方向灌过来，把石桌上那盆还没来得及开花的灵草的叶片边缘拂动了，叶片轻轻摇了两下，又恢复了平静。那盏灯的光正在走下台阶，一步一步地离开观星台的边缘，光在石阶上留下一串正在缩短的暖色光斑，最后消失在拐角处。远处的食堂方向透出一层模糊的暖光，那盏灯和那层暖光正在从两个不同的方向汇向同一个终点。观星台上没有人了。风还在持续地吹过石栏，吹过那盏灯曾经放过的石面。石面上残留着一圈极淡的暖意，正在缓慢地散进风里。
日光从灵晶窗斜照进来，在木地板上铺开一面暖白色的梯形光斑。光斑的边缘正缓慢地朝窗台方向移动——午后的时间正在被它一寸一寸地丈量出来。窗外的灵桂花已经落了大半，剩下几簇还挂在枝头最末端的细枝上，在风里微微晃动，花瓣边缘被日光晒得卷了起来。何天紫坐在窗边的矮榻上，背靠着一只叠好的枕头，膝头摊着那本天机阁古籍。书页仍然停在北斗七星那一页，已经被她翻看了很长时间。她没有在看。
她的目光散着，落在窗外的桂花树冠上，又好像没有落在那里。手指停在页面的边缘，不翻也不握，就那么搭着。午后的光从窗外来，穿过她肩头的衣料、她垂落的发梢、她微微隆起的腹部弧线。房间里面很安静，安静到能听见水烧开后冷却时，水壶底部偶尔发出的金属收缩声——像一枚正在被缓慢冷却的硬币正在收缩它的边缘。
她感觉到了第一次胎动。
那动静从腹部下方靠左的位置传上来，大约在肚脐与耻骨之间——那里是那处比掌心略大一圈的区域，曾因心跳更重而被她反复确认过——一次极轻的、像有什么东西翻了个身。像平静的水面下，一枚光滑的石子被水流缓缓推过，只留下一道几乎看不见的痕迹。她的手指在书页边缘顿住了。拇指按在纸面上，停在那里没有移动。那动静持续了大约两息，然后消失了。她等了一会儿。她把手从书页上抬起来，放在那个位置上——隔着衣料按下去。她等着。呼吸放慢了。
三息过去了。五息过去了。然后那动静又来了。比第一次更清晰，像一枚极小的石子被人从水面下方轻轻推了一下，碰了碰她掌心覆盖着的那个位置，然后退了回去。她的另一只手攥紧了书页边缘，纸面在她指间发出极轻的皱缩声响。她低头看着自己隆起的腹部，目光停在手掌覆盖的那个位置上。
"张德华。"她的声音不高，像一个人在确认一件她已经相信了但还需要另一个人来证实的事。
脚步声从走廊的方向传来。他今天穿了便袍，袖子挽到小臂，手里端着一碗刚切好的灵果。星果的断面在碗沿上泛着水光，汁液的甜味隔着几步远就漫过来了。他的脚步比平时快了大约半拍，像是听见她声音里那个不易察觉的尾音变化——那道尾音微微上挑了一度，。
"怎么了？"他走到矮榻旁边，碗放在旁边的架子上。
何天紫抬头看着他，她的手还放在腹部上方，指尖微微泛白。"你摸——"她的声音不高，尾音正在被压平，但底部浮着一层正在被按住的弧度，"他在动。"
她说完这句话之后，她的目光仍然停留在他脸上，像在确认他是否听懂了。
张德华在矮榻边蹲了下来。他的膝盖先着地，然后另一只膝盖也放下去了。动作不重，不响，但他蹲下来之后的高度和她平齐了。他把手伸过去，放在她腹部上方她手按过的那个位置。他的手指微微张开，掌心朝下，动作轻得像在碰一件正在缓慢成形的东西，一件稍一用力就会留下痕迹的东西。他等在那里，没有动。掌心和她的衣料之间隔着大约一指宽的距离。他等着。
安静持续着。风从窗外灌进来，把他肩头的衣料拂动了一下。远处食堂的油锅声隔着几面墙传过来，闷闷的，像一枚正在被反复捶打的东西。
然后那动静来了。更轻了。像一枚正在确认温度的小东西从他的掌心边缘划过去，停了一下，又划了回来——短促的，带着方向感的，像一个正在寻找位置的人正在用指尖试探周围的轮廓。他的手指蜷了一下。他感觉到了。那透过衣料和皮肤传递上来的颤动，极轻极细，像一枚石子被投进水面的最外层，只留下一圈正在缓慢扩散的痕迹——那痕迹正在向外、向内同时移动着。
他的呼吸变了一拍。然后他开口了，声音不高，像一个人正在对着一面正在缓慢变亮的水面说话，每一个字都落得很轻，像怕惊动什么："你好——"他停了一息，把那个称呼放进去，那两个字落在他和她之间的空气里，像一枚已经确定位置的东西正在被放进它该在的地方，"我是你爸爸。"
他的眼眶泛红了。那道红色从眼睑内侧开始，向眼角方向缓慢蔓延，颜色不深，但持续着，像一滴被稀释过的墨正在纸张的纤维中缓慢渗透。他没有眨眼。目光落在她腹部上方他手掌覆盖的那个位置。
那动静又来了，这一回比之前更轻，但方向变了，像是朝向他手掌的方向靠过来——一枚正在确认方向的信标正在持续地发送它的信号。何天紫靠在枕头上，看着他的侧脸。她没有说话，但她的手从腹部上方移开，放在他搁在她腹部的手背上。他感觉到她掌心的温度——比他手背的温度低大约一两度，但平稳。
四神兽的声音从门外传过来。白虎的脚步声最重，它从走廊东侧跑过来的时候，爪子落在金属地面上的声响像一连串被踩碎的干果壳。然后是青龙，鳞片擦过门框边缘，发出一声极轻的刮擦声。朱雀是从窗户方向落下来的，翅膀收拢时带起的气流把窗台上的花瓣卷起来又放下。玄武是最后到的，慢一些，壳的边缘碰了一下门槛，发出一声短促的、类似木头碰撞的声响。
白虎蹲在门槛外，前爪搭在门框内侧，头微微歪着，金色的眼睛一眨不眨地盯着房间里的方向。张德华侧过头来看了它一眼。白虎的爪子还搭在门框上。他看了它大约两息——那道目光停在白虎的前爪上，像一枚正在被确认位置的钉子——然后他把目光收回来。白虎沉默地缩回了那只前爪，耳朵向后折了半寸，像一面正在被缓慢收拢的旗帜正在从展开状态回到收束状态。

何天紫的低笑声从矮榻的方向传过来。不大，像一枚正在被风推动的铃铛在空气中留下它的回音，只持续了一瞬。她低头看着自己腹部上方他的手，感觉到那层温度正在从他的掌心持续地渗透进她的皮肤。她没有说话。他也蹲在那里，没有站起来。
窗外的桂花，有一朵从末端的细枝上落了，在日光中缓缓地旋转了一圈，落在窗台上。室内的光线正在缓慢地变暖，从午后的白金色过渡到傍晚的暖金色，在地板上的光斑边缘正在变得更加柔和。他的手掌还放在她腹部上方，没有收回去。那动静没有再出现，但他没有移开。他就蹲在那里，等着。
过了很久——可能是半炷香，也可能是一炷香——她开口了："他还不动了。"
"嗯。"
"你可以起来了。"
"——再等一会儿。"
她没有再催他。窗外的天光正在从暖金向橙红过渡，把他蹲在榻边的轮廓镀上了一层正在缓慢加深的暗影。她的指尖仍然搁在他的手背上，沿着他指节的轮廓滑到他的掌心边缘，又收了回去。日光又向西挪了大约一指宽的距离。他还是没有站起来。
晨光从星尘带的边缘切进来，像一把被磨薄了的刀。赤红的光穿过暗色颗粒的缝隙，在平台上投下一道一道平行的亮纹，亮纹的边缘锋利而干燥。平台是三天前搭起来的，铁木的板面被灵能加热过，压平了所有翘起的木刺。但表面仍然残留着一层极细的砂砾——赤火星域的风带来的，贴着板面被踩实了，形成一层硬而脆的壳。
陈铁军站在平台前端，靴底下的砂砾壳正在被他反复踩压，每一次换重心都发出一声极轻的碎裂。他今天换了正式的制式战甲，肩甲上的三枚星徽被擦过，反着光。他身后站着两列上国修士，一共二十四人，每列十二人，间距一致。武器的保险开着——那些灵能步枪的充能指示灯在晨光中亮着稳定的绿光，像一排正在被同时呼吸的眼睛。
他站在那个位置已经站了大约半个时辰。日光从东面过来，把他的影子从身侧拖向西面，在地板上拉成一道细长的暗色轮廓。他的目光锁着前方那片星尘稀疏带的方向，手指垂在身侧，没有握拳。他等了半个时辰，那片稀疏带里除了偶尔被风推着偏移的暗色颗粒之外，什么也没有。
然后他看到了那道光。
从稀疏带的深处来的，先是极淡的一线银白，像有人用针尖在深色的布面上划了一道。然后那线变粗了，变成了一条正在移动的细长光痕。光痕在移动中持续地扩展着自己的宽度，像一枚正在被拉开的卷轴正在从内部向外部延伸它的边缘。陈铁军的瞳孔缩了一下，嘴唇微微张开但没说话。他侧过头朝身后的通道看了一眼，然后转回来，重新锁定了那道正在逼近的光。
银白色战船从星尘稀疏带的外缘切出来的时候，船壳表面的灵能回路纹路正在晨光中闪烁着细密的光。战船的外形修长，没有明显的主炮塔，但船壳表面的灵能回路密度很高——那种排列方式不是为了推进，是为了在瞬间撑开一面足够厚的护盾。它在距离平台约三百丈的地方减速，调整姿态，然后像一枚正在被缓慢放下的金属片一样，平稳地落在平台前方的接驳区上。
舱门打开的声音很轻。像一扇被频繁开关、铰链被反复润滑过的门正在被正常推开，金属与金属接触时发出的是持续而均匀的摩擦声，中间没有卡顿。
使者从舱门里走出来的时候，日光正好落在他身上。他穿了一身银灰色的长袍，袍面的布料没有反光，是一种被刻意处理过的哑光质地。袖口宽大，垂落时布料的褶皱纹路均匀而清晰，像一面正在被缓慢铺开的织物表面。领口压着一枚深紫色的徽章——室女宗的标识，一枚被星环环绕的菱形，中心有一道正在向下延伸的直线。
他的步子不快。每一步落地的时间间隔都相同，大约比正常步速慢了半拍。那种节奏带着一种明确的意图——他在让人看他走近。他走到平台边缘的时候停了一下，目光从陈铁军身上扫过，然后扫过他身后的两列修士。他的目光在那些灵能步枪的充能指示灯上停留了大约一息，然后收回。
陈铁军开口了。他的声音不高，但每一个字都落得稳："室女宗使者？"他问完这五个字之后停住了，等着对方先给出信息。
content_en:
He reached out and picked up the psychic lamp. The heat from the lamp spread through the base into his palm, like a coin being slowly heated. He picked it up and took two steps toward the steps, then stopped and waited for her. She kept pace with him, about half a step behind. Zhang Shanfeng straightened up from the door frame and followed her with the unfinished cup of tea. The four divine beasts stood up from their respective positions in turn, and the white tiger stood up last. It shook its tail when it stood up, and then followed the queue.
The spiritual grass on the observatory was blown by the wind. The wind blew in from the direction of the stardust belt, blowing the edges of the leaves of the pot of spiritual grass on the stone table that had not yet had time to bloom. The leaves shook slightly twice, and then returned to calm. The light of that lamp was walking down the steps, leaving the edge of the observatory step by step. The light left a string of shortening warm-colored spots on the stone steps, and finally disappeared around the corner. A layer of fuzzy warm light shines from the direction of the canteen in the distance. The lamp and the warm light are converging towards the same end point from two different directions. There is no one on the observatory. The wind continued to blow over the stone railing, blowing over the stone surface where the lamp had been. There is a faint warmth remaining on the stone surface, which is slowly dissipating into the wind.
The sunlight shines in obliquely from the spiritual crystal window, spreading a warm white trapezoidal light spot on the wooden floor. The edge of the light spot is slowly moving towards the window sill - the afternoon is being measured inch by inch by it. Most of the osmanthus flowers outside the window have fallen, and a few clusters are still hanging on the twigs at the end of the branches, swaying slightly in the wind, and the edges of the petals are rolled up by the sun. He Tianzi sat on the low couch by the window, leaning on a folded pillow, with the ancient book of Tianji Pavilion spread out on his knees. The page of the book still stopped at the page of the Big Dipper, which she had been looking at for a long time. She wasn't looking.
Her eyes wandered and fell on the crown of osmanthus trees outside the window, but they didn't seem to fall there. His fingers stopped at the edge of the page, not turning or holding it, just resting there. The afternoon light came from the window and passed through the clothing on her shoulders, the tips of her hanging hair, and the slightly bulging curve of her abdomen. The room was very quiet, so quiet that you could hear the occasional metal shrinking sound from the bottom of the kettle when the water cooled after boiling - like a slowly cooling coin shrinking its edges.
She felt her first fetal movement.
The movement came from the lower left side of her abdomen, roughly between her navel and pubic bone—that area was a circle slightly larger than the palm of her hand. She had repeatedly confirmed it due to a heavier heartbeat—a very slight movement, as if something had turned over. Like a smooth stone under the calm water, being slowly pushed by the current, leaving only an almost invisible trace. Her fingers paused on the edge of the page. Press your thumb on the paper and stop there without moving. The movement lasted for about two breaths and then disappeared. She waited for a while. She lifted her hand from the page and placed it there - pressing down through the fabric. She waited. Breathing slowed.
Three breaths passed. Five breaths passed. Then the movement came again. It was clearer than the first time, like a tiny stone being pushed gently from below the water, touching the spot covered by her palm, and then retreated. Her other hand clenched the edge of the page tightly, and the paper made a very slight crinkling sound between her fingers. She looked down at her swollen belly, her eyes stopping at the spot covered by her palms.
"Zhang Dehua." Her voice was low, like someone confirming something that she already believed but needed another person to confirm.
The sound of footsteps came from the direction of the corridor. He was wearing a casual robe today, with his sleeves rolled up to his forearms, and he was holding a bowl of freshly cut spiritual fruits in his hand. The cross-section of the star fruit glistened on the edge of the bowl, and the sweetness of the juice spread over it from a few steps away. His steps were about half a beat faster than usual, as if he heard the sound in her voiceAn imperceptible change in the final sound - the final sound has been raised slightly.
"What's wrong?" He walked to the short couch and placed the bowl on the shelf next to it.
He Tianzi looked up at him, her hand was still on her abdomen, her fingertips were slightly white. "You touch -" her voice was not high-pitched, and the tail tone was being flattened, but there was a layer of arc at the bottom that was being held down, "He is moving."
After she said this, her eyes still stayed on his face, as if to confirm whether he understood.
Zhang Dehua squatted down beside the short couch. His knee hit the ground first, then the other knee came down. The movement wasn't heavy or loud, but when he squatted down he was at the same height as her. He reached over and placed his hand on the spot above her belly where her hand had been. His fingers were slightly open, palm facing down, and his movements were as light as touching something that was slowly taking shape, something that would leave traces with a little force. He waited there without moving. There was about a finger's width between the palm of his hand and the material of her clothes. He waited.
The silence continued. The wind poured in from the window, fluttering the fabric on his shoulders. The sound of the frying pan in the distant cafeteria came through several walls. It was muffled, like an object being beaten repeatedly.
Then the movement came. Lighter. Like a small thing checking the temperature, it swiped across the edge of his palm, paused, and then swiped back again - short, with a sense of direction, like a person who was looking for a location and testing the surrounding contours with his fingertips. His fingers curled up. He felt it. The vibration transmitted through the clothing and skin was extremely light and fine, like a stone thrown into the outermost layer of the water, leaving only a slowly spreading trace - the trace was moving outward and inward at the same time.
His breathing changed. Then he spoke, his voice was low, like a person talking to the slowly brightening water, and every word was spoken very softly, as if he was afraid of disturbing anything: "Hello -" He paused for a breath, and put the title in, and the two words fell in the air between him and her, like an object with a certain position being put into the place where it should be, "I am your father."
His eyes were red. The red color started from the inside of the eyelids and slowly spread toward the corners of the eyes. The color was not deep, but it continued, like a drop of diluted ink slowly seeping into the fibers of the paper. He didn't blink. His eyes fell on the spot above her belly covered by his palm.
The movement came again, this time lighter than before, but the direction changed, as if it was moving towards the direction of his palm - a beacon that was confirming the direction was continuously sending its signal. He Tianzi leaned on the pillow and looked at his profile. She didn't speak, but she moved her hand from above her belly to rest on the back of his hand that was resting on her belly. He felt the temperature in her palm - about a degree or two lower than the temperature on the back of his hand, but steady.
The voices of the four divine beasts came from outside the door. The white tiger's footsteps were the loudest. When it ran from the east side of the corridor, the sound of its claws hitting the metal floor was like a series of crushed dried fruit shells. Then came the green dragon, its scales scraped against the edge of the door frame, making a very light scratching sound. The Suzaku fell from the direction of the window, and the air flow brought up when its wings were folded rolled up and put down the petals on the windowsill. Xuanwu arrived last, slower, and the edge of the shell touched the threshold, making a short sound like the collision of wood.
Bai Hu squatted outside the threshold, his front paws resting on the inside of the door frame, his head tilted slightly, and his golden eyes stared unblinkingly in the direction of the room. Zhang Dehua turned his head and glanced at it. The white tiger's paws were still on the door frame. He looked at it for about two breaths - the gaze rested on the white tiger's front paw, like a nail being confirmed - and then he looked back. The white tiger retracted its front paw silently, earsThe flower was folded back half an inch, like a flag being slowly folded back from its unfolded state to its folded state.
He Tianzi's low laughter came from the direction of the short couch. Not big, like a bell being pushed by the wind, leaving its echo in the air, which lasted only a moment. She looked down at his hand on her abdomen, feeling the warmth from his palm continuing to penetrate into her skin. She said nothing. He also squatted there without standing up.
One of the sweet-scented osmanthus flowers outside the window fell from a twig at the end, slowly spun around in the sunlight, and landed on the windowsill. The light in the room is slowly warming, transitioning from the white gold of the afternoon to the warm gold of the evening, and the edges of the light spots on the floor are becoming softer. His palm was still on her belly and he didn't take it back. The movement didn't happen again, but he didn't move away. He just squatted there, waiting.
After a long time - maybe half a stick of incense, or maybe a stick of incense - she spoke: "He hasn't moved yet."
"Yeah."
"You can get up."
"—Wait a little longer."
She didn't push him anymore. The skylight outside the window was transitioning from warm gold to orange-red, casting a slowly deepening shadow on his silhouette squatting beside the couch. Her fingertips were still resting on the back of his hand, sliding along the outline of his knuckles to the edge of his palm, and then back again. The sun moved westward by about a finger's width. He still didn't stand up.
The morning light cuts in from the edge of the stardust belt, like a sharpened knife. The red light passed through the gaps between the dark particles and cast parallel bright lines on the platform. The edges of the bright lines were sharp and dry. The platform was erected three days ago, and the ironwood boards were heated by psychic energy, flattening all the warped wooden thorns. But there is still a layer of extremely fine gravel left on the surface - brought by the wind from the red Mars domain, it has been trampled firmly against the surface of the board, forming a hard and brittle shell.
Chen Tiejun stood at the front of the platform, the gravel shell under his boots being repeatedly stepped on, and there was a very slight cracking sound every time he changed his weight. He changed into a formal battle armor today, and the three star emblems on the shoulder armor were rubbed and reflected. Behind him stood two rows of monks from the Kingdom of Heaven, a total of twenty-four people, twelve in each row, with the same distance. The weapon's safety was on - the charging indicators of those psychic rifles glowed steadily green in the morning light, like a row of eyes that were being breathed at the same time.
He had been standing in that position for about half an hour. The sunlight came from the east and dragged his shadow from his side to the west, stretching it into a long, dark outline on the floor. His eyes were fixed on the direction of the sparse strip of stardust in front of him, and his fingers were hanging by his sides without making a fist. He waited for half an hour, but there was nothing in that sparse zone except dark particles occasionally pushed away by the wind.
Then he saw the light.
Coming from the depths of the sparse zone, there was first a very faint line of silver, as if someone had scratched a line on the dark cloth with the tip of a needle. Then the line thickened and became a long, moving trail of light. The light traces continue to expand their width as they move, like a scroll being pulled apart and extending its edges from the inside to the outside. Chen Tiejun's pupils shrank, his lips opened slightly but he didn't speak. He turned his head and glanced at the passage behind him, then turned back and locked onto the approaching light again.
When the silver-white warship was cut out from the outer edge of the sparse stardust belt, the psychic circuit patterns on the surface of the hull were shining finely in the morning light. The warship has a slender shape and no obvious main turret, but the density of psychic circuits on the surface of the hull is very high - that arrangement is not for propulsion, but to instantly open up a thick enough shield. It slowed down about three hundred feet away from the platform, adjusted its attitude, and then landed smoothly in front of the platform like a piece of metal being slowly lowered.on the docking area.
The hatch opened softly. Like a door that has been opened and closed frequently and whose hinges have been lubricated repeatedly, it is being pushed open normally. When metal comes into contact with metal, there is a continuous and even friction sound without any jamming.
When the messenger walked out of the hatch, the sun just fell on him. He wore a silver-gray robe. The fabric on the robe was non-reflective and had a deliberately processed matte texture. The cuffs are wide, and the folds of the fabric when hanging down are even and clear, like a fabric surface being slowly spread. There is a dark purple badge on the collar - the symbol of the Maiden Sect, a diamond shape surrounded by a star ring, with a straight line extending downwards in the center.
His pace was slow. The time interval between each step landing is the same, about half a beat slower than the normal pace. That rhythm carried a clear intention - he was letting people watch him approach. When he reached the edge of the platform, he paused and glanced at Chen Tiejun, then at the two rows of monks behind him. His eyes stayed on the charging indicators of those psychic rifles for about a breath, and then he looked back.
Chen Tiejun spoke. His voice was not high, but every word was precise: "Messenger of the Maiden Sect?" He stopped after asking these five words, waiting for the other party to give information first.
